title: First flight (proposed nested types)
source: Charter first-flight.md: power on, connect through a gateway, Takeoff, Move To, Land, with the failure branch. Proposed form from docs/proposals/broad-types.md; not checked against definitions yet.

branches.failsafe: If the link drops during Move To (replaces the main steps after Move To starts)

steps.why: The drone opens the link through the gateway and says which protocol version it speaks.
Core accepts the drone and confirms the version both sides will use.
The drone reports its current settings, so Core knows what it will do if the link drops.
The drone reports it is healthy and ready.
The drone reports where it is on the ground and its battery.
Core sends task 1 of 3 in plan P1: climb straight up to 30 m above home.
Once it holds all 3 tasks of plan P1 (task_count), the drone confirms it is running the plan. Shown here to keep the old order; in a real run it follows the third task.
The drone reports it started T1 (Takeoff).
The drone reports its climb.
The drone reports T1 done: it is holding at 30 m.
Core sends task 2 of 3 in plan P1: fly to a position, keeping the current altitude.
The drone reports it started T2 (Move To).
The drone reports its position and speed on the way.
The drone reports T2 done: it is over the destination.
Core sends task 3 of 3 in plan P1: go to 20 m, fly back over the landing spot and land.
The drone reports it started T3 (Land).
The drone reports it is back on the ground.
The drone reports T3 done. The run is over.
Partway through Move To, the drone loses the gateway and starts its link loss response. It sends this as soon as it can be heard again.
The drone reports T2 failed, so Core's record matches what happened.
The drone cancels the rest of the queue, so T3 (Land) is reported cancelled.
The drone reports its position on the way home.
Nothing marks the end of a run or the Reset ZIP. Not needed on the wire yet; listed so it is not forgotten.
